name: Norclostebol

lead: Norclostebol is a chlorinated derivative of nandrolone, described in 1957 and sold under names such as Lentabol. Physique readers mention it for its anabolic class, reported as strongly anabolic and weakly androgenic.

Wikipedia lists no medical uses. Its acetate ester was reported on the European black market in the late 1990s, and the main published work concerns detecting its illegal use in cattle, including a 2006 study of urinary metabolites. No human studies of muscle or appearance exist.

paras: It has no listed medical use and no established routine.
No human safety studies were found.

angle.text: Norclostebol is a chlorinated nandrolone derivative described in 1957 and reported as strongly anabolic and weakly androgenic, which is why physique readers mention it. It has no listed medical use, and published work mostly concerns detecting it in cattle.

lead: Norclostebol (4-chloro-19-nortestosterone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from nandrolone, sold under names such as Lentabol; its acetate ester has been sold as Anabol 4-19. It was described in the literature in 1957.[1]

Wikipedia lists no medical indications. Its norclostebol acetate form was reported on the European black market in the late 1990s for possible use in livestock, and a 2006 study identified its urinary metabolites in cattle.[1][2]

paras: Wikipedia reports it as strongly anabolic with weaker androgenic activity, estimating about 6.6 times the anabolic and 40 percent of the androgenic potency of testosterone, while noting such comparisons may not be valid and rest on a single citation.[1]
After oral and subcutaneous administration to cattle, the main urinary metabolites were mainly reduced forms, allowing identification of illegal use in animals.[2]

timeline.event: Acetate reported on the European black market for possible use in breeding animals (late 1990s).[2]
